How much does it cost to run an electric blanket?

Electric blankets are one of the cheapest ways to stay warm in bed, because they heat you rather than the room.

Cost per night
7.9p
About £14.37 a year at 2 hours per night, 7 nights a week, 6 months a year.

Standing charge not included.

Adjust for yours
Ofgem price cap average for 1 Oct – 31 Dec 2026 (standard variable tariff, Direct Debit, England, Scotland & Wales).

About these figures

A typical electric blanket uses about 150 watts (40–200W depending on the model). Used for 2 hours per night, 7 nights a week, for 6 months of the year, it costs about 7.9p per night and £14.37 a year at the current price cap rate.

Worth knowing: CSE heating blanket 150W.

Source for the typical figure: CSE 'What uses watt?' table. See how we calculate.

Ways to cut the cost

  • Pre-warm the bed, then switch to low or off.
  • Use a timer or auto-off model.
  • Check the blanket each season for wear, and replace it if wires show or it's over 10 years old.

Questions

How much does it cost to run an electric blanket per hour?

At 26.32p/kWh, a 150W model costs about 3.9p an hour while it's running.

How much does it cost to run an electric blanket per year?

About £14.37 a year, based on 2 hours per night, 7 nights a week, 6 months a year. Change the sliders above to match how you use yours.

Is the standing charge included?

No. You pay the standing charge every day whether or not the appliance is used, so it isn't part of the cost of running it.

How do I find my electric blanket's actual power use?

Check the rating label, plug or manual for the wattage, or the energy label for kWh figures. A plug-in energy monitor shows exactly what it uses.
